method: Each of the 18 TIGHT_GAP_EXECUTOR packages (corpus-passes-v2 L47 screen, P3_SCREENS_V1.json) was adjudicated on the registered demonstrability bar of PASS_L47_V1.md (metadata separation >120 s with ordering and immutability). Two evidence layers beyond the screen were read: (1) per-package full add/modify timelines (triage_timeline_v1.json); (2) CROSS-PACKAGE first-add ordering of producers and consumers (triage_crosspkg_v1.json) - the screen was per-package and could not see these. Semantic layer (freeze-text claims, assay determinism, digest bindings) read per package and cited below. Class MECHANICAL = surviving git metadata demonstrates the package's own frozen claim once cross-package scope, blob pins and digest bindings are read (the screen flag is an artifact of per-package scope and of counting checker/generator .py files as outcome-bearing executors). Class SUBSTANTIVE = the outcome-bearing artifact (or the search implementation the freeze claims to predate) landed inside the 120 s window in the only surviving history; ordering is genuinely non-demonstrable -> prospective re-establishment (W4 pattern).
registered_bar_note: The 120 s bar is the corpus screen's own registered demonstrability threshold (PROSPECTIVE_ORDERED vs TIGHT_GAP_EXECUTOR). This triage neither loosens nor tightens it; it applies the same bar to outcome-bearing artifacts and cross-package chains, which the screen did not read.

KNOWN_FAMILY_BENCHMARK_V1.json has exactly ONE commit (never modified); its git blob 6b9ac309... is pinned by every downstream RESULT (benchmark_blob field). The in-package tight .py (+58 s) is check_aj9a.py, a checker - not the holdout implementation the freeze governs.
